biological.citation: G9a and ZNF644 Physically Associate to Suppress Progenitor Gene Expression during Neurogenesis (PMID: 27546533)
biological.summary: ZNF644 was identified as a G9a/GLP-interacting protein via unbiased affinity purification and mass spectrometry. In zebrafish, znf644a and znf644b orthologs play complementary roles in regulating G9a/H3K9me2-mediated gene silencing during neurogenesis, with non-overlapping requirements during retinal differentiation. ZNF644 is described as a critical co-regulator of G9a/GLP histone methyltransferase activity during neuronal differentiation.

biological.citation: The zinc finger proteins ZNF644 and WIZ regulate the G9a/GLP complex for gene repression (PMID: 25789554)
biological.summary: ZNF644 was identified as a core subunit of the G9a/GLP histone methyltransferase complex through unbiased protein affinity purification. ZNF644 interacts with the transcription activation domain of G9a and contains multiple zinc finger motifs that recognize consensus DNA sequences, targeting G9a to chromatin to mediate H3K9 methylation and gene repression. This study establishes ZNF644 as a key chromatin-targeting subunit of the G9a/GLP complex.

biological.citation: Myopia disease mouse models: a missense point mutation (S673G) and a protein-truncating mutation of the Zfp644 mimic human disease phenotype (PMID: 30834109)
biological.summary: Using TALEN technology, two mouse models were generated carrying either the disease-associated missense mutation Zfp644 S673G or a truncated form (Zfp644 Δ8). Both mutants showed significant differences in vitreous chamber depth and lens diameter consistent with high myopia, while retinal physiological function was preserved. These models confirm that ZNF644/Zfp644 mutations are causative for ocular changes associated with high myopia.

biological.citation: miR-362 regulates the proliferation and apoptosis of porcine immature Sertoli cells through targeting the ZNF644 gene (PMID: 30021720)
biological.summary: miR-362 was shown to directly target the 3'UTR of ZNF644 in porcine immature Sertoli cells, suppressing its expression as confirmed by dual luciferase reporter assay. Overexpression of miR-362 or knockdown of ZNF644 arrested cells in G1 and G2 phases, inhibited proliferation, and enhanced apoptosis. These results indicate ZNF644 plays a role in Sertoli cell survival and cell cycle progression during spermatogenesis.

biological.citation: A Massively Parallel Screen of 5'UTR Mutations Identifies Variants Impacting Translation and Protein Production in Neurodevelopmental Disorder Genes (PMID: 37961498)
biological.summary: A high-throughput assay screening 5'UTR patient mutations identified variants in ZNF644 that specifically alter translational activity in neurons in vivo. Patient-derived cell line studies confirmed that these 5'UTR mutations can alter ZNF644 protein production in individuals with autism. This implicates ZNF644 as a gene whose dysregulation via 5'UTR mutations may contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders.

biological.citation: Study of a US cohort supports the role of ZNF644 and high-grade myopia susceptibility (PMID: 22539872)
biological.summary: Sanger sequencing of ZNF644 coding regions in 131 high-grade myopia cases identified two novel variants (c.725C>T, c.821A>T) not found in 672 ethnically matched controls. A rare variant (rs12117237) was present in 6 cases and 5 controls. The study supports a role for ZNF644 variants in myopia susceptibility in a US cohort including Caucasian and African American individuals.

biological.citation: CD4 T-cell transcriptome analysis reveals aberrant regulation of STAT3 and Wnt signaling pathways in rheumatoid arthritis: evidence from a case-control study (PMID: 25880754)
biological.summary: Whole-genome transcriptome profiling of CD4 T cells from 53 RA patients and 45 healthy controls identified ZNF644 as one of several differentially expressed zinc finger transcription factors confirmed in a validation cohort. ZNF644 expression was aberrant in RA patient CD4 T cells, suggesting it may be a potential pathogenic factor in rheumatoid arthritis. The study highlights ZNF644 alongside ZEB1 and ZNF292 as dysregulated zinc finger transcription factors in RA.

biological.citation: Gene expression differences in PTSD are uniquely related to the intrusion symptom cluster: A transcriptome-wide analysis in military service members (PMID: 31039430)
biological.summary: Transcriptome-wide analysis of peripheral blood in military service members identified ZNF644 as one of 10 genes upregulated in participants with PTSD and high intrusion symptoms at baseline and downregulated following successful sleep-based treatment. ZNF644 upregulation was specifically associated with the intrusion symptom cluster rather than other PTSD symptom clusters. This positions ZNF644 as a potential molecular biomarker for PTSD intrusion symptoms and treatment response.
biological.sample_size: 39 PTSD participants, 22 with high intrusion symptoms

biological.citation: Developing ZNF Gene Signatures Predicting Radiosensitivity of Patients with Breast Cancer (PMID: 34504527)
biological.summary: Analysis of 976 breast cancer samples from TCGA revealed that high expression of ZNF644 was associated with radiosensitivity in breast cancer patients. A 4-gene ZNF signature including ZNF644 (high expression) and three other ZNF genes (low expression) predicted better overall survival following radiotherapy, validated in the METABRIC database. ZNF644 is proposed as a component of a radiosensitivity gene signature for breast cancer.

biological.citation: The expanding role of the Ehmt2/G9a complex in neurodevelopment (PMID: 28596979)
biological.summary: This review highlights ZNF644 as a recently characterized context-dependent binding partner of the Ehmt1/2 (G9a/GLP) complex that coordinates its activity during early neurodevelopment. ZNF644 is discussed as part of the mechanism by which the G9a/GLP complex achieves tissue- and temporal-specific H3K9 methylation and gene repression. The review frames ZNF644 as a key regulator of G9a/GLP function in the neurodevelopmental epigenetic landscape.
